صُفَّاحٌ ; and its n. un., with ة: see صَفِيحَةٌ, in five places. ―
-b2- Also (tropical:) Camels whose humps have become large, (K, TA,) so that the hump of the she-camel occupies the whole of her back: n. un. with ة: (TA:) pl. صُفَّاحَاتٌ and صَفَافِيحُ: (K:) likened to wide, or broad, stones or similar things, because of their hardness. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
